findings.title: include_website_name is missing the required '?' suffix, so it is never invoked
findings.body: The method `include_website_name` (lines 153-155) is meant to control whether `website_name` is serialized, based on `website.present?`. Every other conditional-inclusion method in this file follows the `include_<attr>?` naming convention (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_user_fields?`), which the serializer framework looks up by that exact name. Because this new method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, the framework never finds/calls it, so `website_name` is always serialized — even when the user has no website set, in which case it will be emitted as `null`. This silently breaks the intended 'only include when present' behavior and adds a useless field to every user payload.

findings.title: website_name is not covered by the untrusted_attributes restriction that hides website for low-trust/anonymous viewers
findings.body: The raw `website` attribute is passed to `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), which hides it from anonymous visitors viewing a TL0 user via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. The new derived attribute `website_name` (added to the attributes list and implemented at line 137) is not added to this list, so it has no such restriction and is controlled only by the broken `include_website_name` check (see other finding). As a result, even when `website` is correctly hidden from a restricted viewer, `website_name` — which exposes the domain, and, when domains match, the full path derived from the same website value — is still serialized, leaking information that the `website` restriction was meant to hide.

findings.title: untrusted_attributes test does not cover the new website_name attribute
findings.body: The spec list at line 11 enumerates attributes expected to be hidden from anonymous TL0 viewers, but it was not updated to include `:website_name` even though this PR introduces that attribute as a direct derivative of the restricted `:website` field. Because of this omission, the existing 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' test does not catch that `website_name` is unconditionally serialized and bypasses the trust-level restriction applied to `website` (see related serializer findings).

findings.title: Domain comparison in website_name is case-sensitive
findings.body: In `website_name` (lines 137-151), `website_host` (parsed from the user-supplied `website` URL) is compared against `discourse_host` (`Discourse.current_hostname`) using plain string equality and `ends_with?` without normalizing case. Host names are case-insensitive, so a website entered as e.g. 'Example.com' when the instance hostname is 'example.com' (or vice versa) will fail to match even though the domains are effectively identical, causing the UI to show only the bare host instead of the intended full path.
